newsitem.title: USA: CBOT July soy ends limit-down on Brazil imports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT July soy ends limit-down on Brazil imports.

text.p: CBOT July soybean futures ended limit-down Wednesday on confirmation that Cargill Inc was importing Brazilian soybeans to process in its southeastern U.S. crushing plants, traders and analysts said.

"They've been able to buy these beans because of the lower prices of beans in South America, said Dale Durchholz, analyst with Agrivisor Services in Bloomington, Ill. "It's going to be negative for the market."
Cargill released a statement Wednesday saying record-tight U.S. soybean supplies forced them to turn to Brazil for soybeans to crush.

Cargill would not specify the quantity it was going to import, but market rumors pegged it at four cargos or approximately 200,000 tonnes. Shipping sources said Cargill had already fixed two cargos into the U.S. Gulf.
However, world and U.S. demand for soybeans remained strong, so the impact of the Brazil imports on U.S. supplies should be relatively small, analysts and traders said.
"What they are importing really shouldn't influence the balance sheet," said one floor trader.
CBOT soybeans ended 30 cents to 8-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 30 cents at $8.30 per bushel.
Traders also cited severe technical weakness in July soybeans as a source of the selloff.
A close below $8.31-3/4 in July soybeans was seen as the completion of a right shoulder in a bearish head and shoulders formation, technicians said.
After Wednesday's close at $8.30, the next downward objective for some technicians is seen at $7.58 per bushel in July.
Liquidation in the July contract also continued following some cash merchandisers' decisions on Tuesday to quote bids basis November rather than July CBOT futures.
"With the cash guys switching the basis, nobody wants to trade in July and nobody wants to be long in July," said one veteran trader.
On the day, funds sold at least 25 million bushels of soybeans. ING and Iowa Grain each sold four million July and Smith Barney sold 13 million July and two million August.
In options trade, Lind Waldock bought 500 November $8.25 calls and sold 500 September $8.50 calls, pit sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 100,000 contracts. That figure compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 68,411.
